patients.summary: Healthy landscaper who joined in 2024, then suffered full-thickness circumferential leg burns in a house fire in August 2025 with compartment syndrome treated by fasciotomies and grafting. In summer 2026 a changing left forearm lesion proved to be a stage IB melanoma, treated with wide excision and a negative sentinel node biopsy.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to establish with us. 39 y/o, landscaping business, says his last PCP retired and he never got matched with anyone. BCBS PPO, card info entered. No active issues. Booked new pt physical 9/10 at 8:00, early because he's on a job site by 9. Records release sent by email for prior office.

orders.order: Request records from prior primary care office

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Connor is a 39-year-old man joining the practice. Runs a small landscaping and lawn crew, outdoors most of the year. Previous PCP retired a couple of years ago and he has not had a checkup since. No complaints today.

PMH: none. PSH: none. Meds: none, occasional ibuprofen after a long day. Allergies: none known.
FH: father died of melanoma, diagnosed in his mid-50s. Mother has type 2 diabetes. Paternal uncle had a basal cell skin cancer.
SH: single, lives in Greenfield. Never smoked. A beer or two most weeks. No drug use. Wears a hat at work, admits sunscreen is hit or miss.

ROS negative in full.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Well appearing, fit. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement or nodes. Lungs clear. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities warm, no edema, pulses 2+. Skin: tanned forearms and neck. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P: healthy adult, establishing care.
- Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c given mother's diabetes. One-time HIV and hep C screening, he agrees.
- Talked about daily sunscreen on exposed skin and long sleeves in peak months given the family history and his job.
- PHQ-2 negative.
- Flu and COVID vaccines once the fall supply comes in; RN visit.
- Records requested from prior office.
Return in a year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Connor, your bloodwork is all normal. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol and A1c are where we like them, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Received 14 pages from prior PCP office, scanned to media. Visits 2016 to 2021, mostly annual physicals and one visit for a sprained wrist in 2019. Labs from 2021 normal. No problem list entries. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in after work for flu and COVID. No prior reactions. Flu 0.5 mL IM right deltoid, COVID 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. VIS given. Waited 15 min, no problems. Left with a reminder to call if fever or arm swelling beyond a day or two.

Full-thickness burn of right lower leg
Full-thickness burn of left lower leg

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, burn center. Date of service 08/02/2025.

Arrived by ambulance after fire crews pulled him out of a burning house. Both lower legs burned all the way around. Complaining of severe leg pain; IV morphine given en route and again here with little effect. Otherwise healthy, takes nothing, no drug allergies. Never smoker, light drinker, works in landscaping.

VS on arrival: BP 130/85, HR 110, RR 22, T 37.2 C (99.0 F). On oxygen by non-rebreather from the field, talking in full sentences, no stridor, no hoarseness. Airway inspected and patent.

Legs: circumferential burns of both lower legs, knee to ankle. Skin is white, leathery and insensate in the burned areas, consistent with full-thickness injury. Compartments tense on both sides. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses diminished bilaterally. Cannot move his toes. Upper extremities, trunk and face without burns.

Labs: Hgb 14.5, WBC 16.0, Plt 250, Na 140, K 4.2, Cr 1.0, BUN 18.

ED course: aggressive fluid resuscitation started. Tdap given. Oxygen continued, he stayed comfortable without need for intubation. Burn surgery at bedside within the hour.

Impression: circumferential full-thickness burns of both lower legs with acute compartment syndrome; smoke inhalation exposure.
Disposition: to OR emergently for escharotomies and fasciotomies, then admit to the burn unit.

Allergies: NKDA.

medications.drug: acetaminophen 325 MG / oxycodone hydrochloride 5 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain

documents.title: Operative report: bilateral escharotomies and fasciotomies (received)
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital burn service. Date of surgery 08/02/2025.
Preoperative and postoperative diagnosis: circumferential full-thickness burns of both lower legs with acute compartment syndrome.
Procedure: escharotomies of both lower legs; four-compartment fasciotomies of both lower legs through medial and lateral incisions.
Anesthesia: general.
Findings: tense compartments on both sides. After release, all muscle groups contracted to stimulation and looked viable. Foot pulses improved at the end of the case.
Wounds dressed open with antimicrobial dressings. EBL minimal. No complications. To burn ICU in stable condition.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Burn unit discharge summary (received)
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital burn unit. Admitted 08/02/2025, discharged 08/22/2025.

Reason for admission: circumferential full-thickness burns of both lower legs from a house fire, with compartment syndrome on arrival; smoke exposure.

Course: emergency escharotomies and bilateral four-compartment fasciotomies the day of admission. Resuscitated per protocol. Smoke exposure managed with oxygen only; never intubated, weaned to room air the next morning. On 08/08 he returned to the OR for excision of the leg burns and split-thickness skin grafting, which also covered the fasciotomy wounds. Donor sites both thighs. Graft take excellent at the first and second dressing changes. Toe movement and sensation returned after the release and were normal at discharge. Worked with PT daily; walking with a walker, then a cane by the end of the stay.

Discharge medications: oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325, 1 to 2 tabs every 6 hours as needed, #30, no refills. Moisturizer to healed areas.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: burn clinic in about 3 weeks with dressing teaching done; outpatient PT for knee and ankle motion and gait; PCP within a week. Off work until cleared by burn clinic.

documents.title: Call from hospital case manager
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Case manager from the burn unit called to let us know Connor was admitted Saturday after a house fire, burns to both legs, already had surgery to release the leg compartments and is stable on the floor. Grafting planned later this week. Asked them to fax records at discharge. PCP aware. Will book hospital follow-up once discharge date is known.

conditions.label: Acute compartment syndrome of lower extremity due to circumferential full-thickness burns

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 5 days after discharge from the burn unit. Burn unit discharge summary and op notes reviewed.

Recap: house fire 8/2 with full-thickness burns around both lower legs and compartment syndrome; same-day escharotomies and fasciotomies, then excision and grafting 8/8. Oxygen only for the smoke, no breathing trouble since.

Now: walks in with a cane. Pain is a 3-4 most of the day, worse after dressing changes. Using the oxycodone mostly at night, about 2 a day, plans to taper off. Sleeping in pieces. No fever, no drainage he's worried about. Toes move fine, feeling is normal. Breathing normal, no cough. A friend is driving him and helping with groceries.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet, afebrile. Lungs clear. Both lower legs in clean dressings from knee to ankle; thigh donor sites dry, healing. Feet warm, cap refill brisk, toes move fully, light touch intact. Calves soft above the dressings.

A/P:
1. Full-thickness leg burns s/p excision and grafting: healing per plan. Burn clinic 9/3 area, PT starting. Bowel regimen while on oxycodone; acetaminophen during the day; goal off opioid in 1-2 wks. No refill today.
2. Compartment syndrome s/p fasciotomies: treated, neurovascular exam normal. Off active list.
3. Smoke exposure: no residual symptoms.
4. Mood: rough few weeks, PHQ-2 1. He knows he can reach me any time.
CBC and BMP today. Work note given, out until burn clinic clears him.

documents.title: Work status note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To whom it may concern: Connor Warner is under medical care following a hospitalization and is unable to work at this time. Expected return will be determined by his surgical team. Please contact the office with questions.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Connor, yesterday's blood counts and kidney tests came back normal. No anemia after all of that, which is good news for healing.

events.reason: Gait and range of motion after leg burns

documents.title: Physical therapy evaluation (received)
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient PT evaluation 09/03/2025. Dx: s/p bilateral lower leg burns with escharotomies, fasciotomies and grafting.
Subjective: walks with a cane, stiff in the mornings, wants to get back to work on a crew. Pain 3/10.
Objective: ankle motion stiff at end range both sides, knees full. Gait slowed, uses cane. Grafts intact, no open areas.
Plan: 2x/week for 8 weeks, stretching, scar mobility once cleared, gait training, return-to-work conditioning. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Disability forms
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I have a short term disability policy through my business insurance and they sent a form that needs a doctor to fill out. Should it go to you or the burn people? Can drop it off Monday.

documents.title: RE: Disability forms
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Connor, either works, but since the burn clinic is setting your return date they are the best ones to complete it. If they won't, drop it here and Dr. will fill it out using their notes. Turnaround is about a week.

documents.title: Burn clinic follow-up letter (received)
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body:
Dear colleague,
I saw Mr. Warner in burn clinic on 10/22/2025, eleven weeks after his leg burns and fasciotomies and ten weeks after grafting. He is off all pain medication and walking without the cane. PT reports steady gains.
On exam the grafts on both lower legs are fully healed and stable, no open areas. The thigh donor sites have healed. Ankles move well. Feet warm with normal pulses and sensation.
Plan: custom compression garments to both lower legs, worn daily for the next year; moisturizer and sun protection over the grafts. He may return to light duty now, avoiding heavy lifting and long periods on uneven ground, and full duty from January 2026. Clinic again in 3 months.
Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Burn surgery attending

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu and COVID boosters. Tolerated both last year, just a sore arm. Flu IM R deltoid, COVID IM L deltoid, lots in the vaccine record. Observed 15 minutes, fine. He mentioned he is back on light duty at work this week.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Big year: fire in August with burns to both legs, fasciotomies and grafting, now healed per burn clinic. Doing light duty, mostly running the crew and estimates, back to full work in January. Wears compression sleeves daily. No pain meds. Sleeping well again. Mood good, PHQ-9 is 2.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA. FH unchanged. Never smoker, 1-2 drinks a week.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen benign. Both lower legs with healed grafts from knee to ankle, well adhered, no open areas, compression garments on; healed donor sites on both thighs. Feet warm, pulses intact, sensation normal. Gait normal.

A/P:
- Healed leg burns: follows with burn clinic. Graft and general sun protection reviewed; with his work and his dad's history he should look at his skin and tell me about any spot that changes.
- Prevention: flu and COVID done in October, Tdap given in the ED in August. CMP, lipids, A1c today.
- Return in a year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Connor, everything from Wednesday is normal: kidney and liver function, sugar, A1c and cholesterol. Have a good winter.
